links.outcome: AI fall risk model AUROC versus rule-based clinical systems on same data
links.effect: AI models consistently outperformed rule-based systems in all setups; AUROC 0.735 (90% CI 0.727-0.744) geriatric hospital, 0.926 (90% CI 0.924-0.928) university hospital.
links.quote: Our findings demonstrate that AI models consistently outperform rule-based systems across all experimental setups, with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.735 (90% CI 0.727-0.744) for the geriatric hospital, and 0.926 (90% CI 0.924-0.928) for the university hospital.

links.outcome: Generalization of models across hospitals with demographic and label distribution differences
links.effect: Demographic shifts and label distribution imbalances limited federated learning models' ability to generalize; FL did not improve fall risk prediction.
links.quote: However, it also reveals the challenges related to demographic shifts and label distribution imbalances, which limited the FL models' ability to generalize.

links.outcome: Model fairness across sex and age subgroups
links.effect: No performance disparities between sex groups, but fairness infringements found across age groups.
links.quote: Our fairness analysis ruled out disparities in model performance between different sex groups, but we found fairness infringements across age groups.

unlisted_practices: federated learning across hospitals to train models without sharing data

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of fall risk predictive models comparing centralized training vs. federated learning across two hospital datasets and evaluating demographic fairness, without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or workflow safeguard.
